'''Jonathan Nesbit Coleman''' is the [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Natural and Experimental Philosophy]] in the School of Physics and a Principal Investigator in [[CRANN]] and the AMBER Research Centre at [[Trinity College Dublin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcd.ie/physics/people/academic/|title= Academic/Research Staff, School of Physics|website=Trinity College Dublin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/thin-materials-could-widen-energy-storage-1.1518517|title=Thin materials could widen energy storage|last=O'Connell|first=Claire|date=2013-09-09|newspaper=The Irish Times|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-04-25}}</ref> Coleman's research focuses on solution-processing of nanomaterials and their use in applications. He has worked on [[liquid phase exfoliation]], a widely used method of preparing two-dimensional [[nanosheet]]s.<ref name="tabor">{{cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/2022-david-tabor-medal-and-prize|title= 2022 David Tabor Medal and Prize|website=Institute of Physics}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Coleman attended the [[King's Hospital School]], before studying for a BA in experimental physics in Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/quantum-humour-beams-back-after-absence-1.503342|title='Quantum humour' beams back after absence|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref> He completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics in TCD in 1999 under Professor [[Werner J. Blau|Werner Blau]].<ref name="tcdprofile">{{cite web|url=https://www.tcd.ie/research/profiles/?profile=colemaj|title=Trinith Research: Professor Jonathan Coleman|website=Trinity College Dublin}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Coleman became a lecturer in physics at TCD in 2001 rising to Professor of Chemical Physics (2011 - 2022) and later Erasmus Smith's Professor (2022 - present).<ref name="tcdprofile"/> He is currently (2022) the Head of the School of Physics in TCD and a member of the University Council.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcd.ie/committeepapers/council/membership/|title=Membership - University Council Papers - Trinity College Dublin|website=www.tcd.ie}}</ref>

The theme of his research is the production and processing of [[nanomaterials]] in liquids. The main focus is [[liquid phase exfoliation]] of layered crystals such as [[graphite]] and inorganic layered compounds. This produces liquid [[Suspension (chemistry)|suspensions]] of two-dimensional nanosheets such as [[graphene]], [[Boron nitride|BN]], [[Molybdenum disulfide|MoS<sub>2</sub>]] or [[Molybdenum trioxide|MoO<sub>3</sub>]]. He has also performed research on other nanomaterials such as [[carbon nanotubes]] and metallic [[nanowire]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1557/mrs.2011.236|title=The effects of percolation in nanostructured transparent conductors|first1=Sukanta|last1=De|first2=Jonathan N.|last2=Coleman|date=1 October 2011|journal=MRS Bulletin|volume=36|issue=10|pages=774–781|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1557/mrs.2011.236|bibcode=2011MRSBu..36..774D |hdl=2262/66861 |s2cid=135474225 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>

Coleman's papers have been cited 120,000 times yielding a h-index of 125.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8PCLjvYAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Jonathan N Coleman}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
In 2005, Coleman was elected a fellow of Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-05-10 |title=Trinity Monday 2005 - Fellows and Scholars |url=https://www.tcd.ie/Secretary/FellowsScholars/2005/index.php |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=Trinity College Dublin |archive-date=14 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414165706/https://www.tcd.ie/Secretary/FellowsScholars/2005/index.php |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> Coleman was named the 2011 [[Science Foundation Ireland]] Researcher of the Year<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcd.ie/news_events/articles/trinity-nanoscientist-awarded-science-foundation-ireland-researcher-of-the-year-award/|title=Trinity Nanoscientist Awarded Science Foundation Ireland Researcher of the Year Award|last=|first=|date=2011-11-15|website=Trinity College Dublin|language=en-GB|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-04-25}}</ref> and was awarded the Kroll Medal from the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining|Institute of Materials]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iom3.org/award-winners-2012|title=Award winners 2012|last=|first=|date=|website=IOM3|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-04-25}}</ref> In 2018 he was named the ''[[ACS Nano]]'' Lecture Awardee by the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Announcing the 2018 ACS Nano Award Lecture Laureates|first1=Sergey N.|last1=Shmakov|first2=Paul S.|last2=Weiss|date=26 June 2018|journal=ACS Nano|volume=12|issue=6|pages=5067–5068|doi=10.1021/acsnano.8b04497|pmid=29911860 |s2cid=49268465 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and in 2022 was awarded the Tabor Medal by the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name="tabor"/> In 2023, he received the Royal Irish Academy Gold Medal in the Physical and Mathematical Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-30 |title=Jonathan N. Coleman MRIA |url=https://www.ria.ie/grants-awards/awards/gold-medals/gold-medal-recipients/jonathan-n-coleman-mria/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=Royal Irish Academy |language=en}}</ref> He is also a [[Member of the Royal Irish Academy]] (MRIA),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ria.ie/jonathan-nesbit-coleman|title=Jonathan Nesbit Coleman|date=19 October 2015|website=Royal Irish Academy}}</ref> a Member of the European Academy of Sciences (EURASC),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/|title=Members |website=European Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
